corpus.text: The application is divided into CLI, MCP service, retrieval, trust, and storage modules.
The retrieval path embeds the query, searches dense and sparse indexes, fuses candidates, and optionally reranks them.
The trust layer evaluates provenance, calibration, validity, and supersession before an answer is admitted.
The MCP transport verifies tokens, isolates tenants, enforces scopes, applies rate limits, and executes tools.
The PostgreSQL store provides vector search, lexical search, metadata filtering, and tenant row policies.
Fast retrieval disables reranking and uses a bounded admission queue for low latency service.
Quality retrieval enables the pinned local cross encoder and uses a separate concurrency budget.
Cold requests include model and connection initialization while warm requests measure the steady state.
A refused request is counted as an explicit error and must not be silently dropped or retried.
Performance artifacts record the commit, corpus digest, query digest, host, profile, and stage timings.
Fail closed means an unavailable safety decision refuses to serve an untrusted result.
Fail open is reserved for optional hooks where an integration failure must not interrupt the user session.
Cleanup only catches release failures after the primary operation and still attempts every cleanup step.
Error translation exposes a stable application error without leaking provider exception details.
Broad exception handlers declare their policy beside the handler so reviewers can audit the boundary.
Architecture freshness checks keep generated module maps aligned with the import graph.
Mutation testing targets trust, MCP server, generation administration, and provenance control safety paths.
Optional import checks exercise each declared installation profile independently in CI.
A serial regression run is useful on hosts where parallel workers exhaust native thread limits.
The codebase uses explicit seams so retrieval and generation administration can be extracted safely.
